clue.text: One has good reason for making this journey

definitions.text: One has good reason for making this journey

parts.words: One has good reason for making this journey
parts.note: a devout traveller sets out for a holy shrine with a pious purpose, so the reason is good in the moral sense as well as sound

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a trip with a sound motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good reason' reads as a sensible motive, but the cryptic sense is a religious one: the journey is made for the sake of the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to a sacred place undertaken for devotional reasons is the classic religious trip.

definitions.meaning: to keep food in vinegar or brine

explanation.surface: Something saved from a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to conserve food in brine and a tricky situation, a mess.

indicators.note: seized means the animal holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: round signals that the artist abbreviation is turned about

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A wild creature grabbed a painter by the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns RA into AR, which 'seized' places inside LYNX. 'Throat' is a loose definition: the voice box sits in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box is the organ in the upper windpipe, part of the neck's interior.

clue.text: Get up bright but not necessarily early

definitions.text: Get up bright but not necessarily early

parts.words: Get up bright but not necessarily early
parts.note: the phrase is a cheerful command to leave bed and be lively, though it says nothing of the hour

explanation.walkthrough: The jolly wake-up call tells the sleeper to get up and look lively, but the words do not say when.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional cheery morning call ordering someone out of bed.

indicators.note: to include tells us the word for lunatic holds another letter

parts.note: mad means lunatic
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A crazy person is said to take in an unmarried young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' suggests an unmarried girl, but it simply gives I, which goes inside MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

parts.note: the clue points to the comic operetta by W S Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan about Venetian oarsmen

explanation.walkthrough: The Gondoliers is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, a staple of British amateur stages; its title characters row boats in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Venetian boatmen who pole their craft along the canals, the title characters of the Savoy opera.

clue.text: Go away, not right to include confidence trick

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for right from the word meaning go away

parts.note: scram is a slangy order to go away

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off for dishonestly taking part in a confidence trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from SCRAM, leaving the four letters; 'to include' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle that tricks a victim who trusts the fraudster.

clue.text: Overdrawn in the channel islands, Edward put money on one side of the account

definitions.text: put money on one side of the account

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy
being in the red means overdrawn at the bank
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward, overdrawn while living in Jersey, deposits cash into his bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: RED sits inside CI, then TED follows. The credit side of a ledger is one side of the account.
explanation.definitionFit: To be credited is to have a sum entered on the receiving side of a ledger.

clue.text: Think of yours truly, I had turned up at the gallery

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying me

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the contraction is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on themselves after appearing at an art museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ID into DI in this down clue; 'of' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect deeply or contemplate.

indicators.note: following places the letter for one after the word for a believer

parts.note: a Christian is a believer in the faith
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A woman described as a devotee of some faith.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRISTIANA is the wife of Christian in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, hence 'Lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Christiana is a woman's name, most famously the heroine of the second part of Bunyan's allegory.

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five, the number in a quintet

indicators.note: off suggests the word led is spoiled or out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Five performers set out across open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LED as ELD, which follows V. Veld is the open country of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The veld is the open, grassy plain of South Africa.

indicators.note: into tells us the rearranged letters go inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: struggles suggests the letters of sightseer writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist wrestles with getting into a car until it finally works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like 'until' but is the noun, a shop's cash drawer. 'struggles' rearranges SIGHTSEER as ASHREGISTE, which 'into' puts inside CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the machine in a shop that records sales and holds the money.

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the word for a ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece aboard an ocean liner is flat in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-dimensional' looks like a criticism of the article, but it is the definition: A goes inside LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that extends only along a straight line has just one dimension.

indicators.note: reform means re-form, so the letters of mortals and I are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A preacher declares that sinful humans will be improved by him.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: one who says 'I reform mortals' is a preacher of conduct, and 'reform' rearranges MORTALS I.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralizer seeks to improve the behaviour of people by lecturing them on right and wrong.

parts.note: the opposite of against is in favour of, the preposition for
the opposite of none is all
the opposite of this is that, the pointer to something further off

explanation.surface: Despite everything, someone opposes not a bit of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is replaced by its opposite: 'against' gives FOR, 'none' gives ALL, 'this' gives THAT, with 'of' along for the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless or despite that, the sense of notwithstanding.

clue.text: Had moments in suffering severe reprimand

indicators.note: suffering implies the letters of had moments in are distressed and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone endured some painful times during a harsh telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges all twelve letters of HAD MOMENTS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuke or stern warning given to correct someone's conduct.

clue.text: Stress identification was included for mishap

indicators.note: was included tells us identification goes inside the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is the stress laid on a syllable

explanation.surface: Anxiety about papers came along with an unfortunate mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' suggests worry, but it is emphasis in speech: ACCENT holds ID.
explanation.definitionFit: An unforeseen unlucky event causing damage or injury is an accident.

clue.text: Father's second volume containing record of transactions

parts.note: pa is father, and with the possessive it gives pa's
a book is a volume

explanation.surface: Dad's second book contains his banking records.
explanation.walkthrough: A passbook is the small book a bank or building society gives a saver; 'containing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank or building-society booklet in which deposits and withdrawals are entered for the saver.

clue.text: Hit obstacle used as safety device

parts.note: to crash is to hit violently
a barrier is an obstacle in the way

explanation.surface: Something that blocks the way is struck, yet serves to protect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used as' only links the wordplay to the definition. The answer is the guard rail along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside rail or fence that stops vehicles leaving the carriageway protects drivers.

clue.text: Brother within minute, say, produced tonal quality

indicators.note: within shows the abbreviation for brother goes inside the other word

parts.note: a minute is an example of a unit of time

explanation.surface: A monk's brief moment yielded a pleasant sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks minute as an example, giving TIME, with BR placed inside it; 'produced' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the characteristic colour of a sound that distinguishes one instrument or voice from another.

definitions.meaning: a break from work, as when Parliament or school stops sitting
an alcove or niche set back in a wall

explanation.surface: A holiday spent in a cosy corner?
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a break when a legislature or school is not sitting and an alcove in a wall.

clue.text: Linen, say, had been arranged in a crazy manner

indicators.note: had been arranged tells us the letters of linen and say are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Bed sheets were laid out in a wild fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it introduces an example, but it is part of the fodder: LINEN SAY rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something madly is acting like a person out of their mind.

indicators.note: first takes the opening of the word violet, here its first two letters

parts.note: to rile is to annoy

explanation.surface: An irritable Violet goes first, demanding to know which man is the tough one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violet first' gives VI, the start of violet, placed before RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile describes a man who is strongly masculine and vigorous.

indicators.note: incompletely says the word for tanned is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: someone tanned has gone brown in the sun

explanation.surface: A forehead only partly bronzed by the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incompletely' drops the final N of BROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow is the area of the face above the eyes.

indicators.note: reversible is used for the word for a gown being read backwards

parts.note: a robe is a long gown

explanation.surface: A garment that can be worn inside out comes from a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor, short for the Latin Eboracum, means 'of York', as in the Archbishop of York's signature and the Ebor Handicap horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived abbreviation names things belonging to the northern English city.

clue.text: Like gift of new chair by board

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of chair are made into something fresh

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a festive board

explanation.surface: A present resembling a freshly made chair placed beside a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CHAIR as CHARI, followed by TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation to a good cause is described as being of a benevolent kind.

clue.text: Accept sequence of film photographed at one time

definitions.meaning: to receive or agree to something offered

definitions.text: sequence of film photographed at one time
definitions.meaning: a single uninterrupted shot recorded by the camera in movie-making

explanation.surface: A film director agrees to use one continuous shot.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to receive and a single filmed shot in a movie studio.

parts.note: high-flying normally means very successful, but here the servant literally works in the air aboard an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flying' suggests an ambitious high achiever; it is literal, a cabin crew member on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who looks after passengers on an airliner is a cabin crew member.
